question.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $C(2,50,-19)$ and is parallel to the lines $\mathbf{r}= \langle 2,\sqrt{6},17 \rangle + s \langle -1,7,2 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{r}= \langle 20,-44, 27 \rangle + t \langle 2\sqrt{3},9,-8 \rangle$.
question.worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are $\mathbf{v_1}=\langle  -1,7,2  \rangle$ and $\mathbf{v_2}=\langle 2\sqrt{3},9,-8 \rangle$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $C(2,50,-19)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $\mathbf{c}=\langle 2,50,-19 \rangle.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =c+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨2,50,-19⟩+s\,⟨-1,7,2⟩+t\,⟨2\sqrt{3},9,-8⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )\end{aligned}
$$
